copy.blurb:
This is a Pick. Switzerland v Canada in FIFA World Cup 2026 on Wednesday, and the model and the market disagree on the Canada side by +15.0pp. That's the gap the verdict rests on.

The Elo prior reads Switzerland 1830 vs Canada 1860: 30 points in favour of Canada, which is a meaningful but not decisive prior. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Switzerland to win at 33%, the draw at 28%, and Canada to win at 39%. Each number is a probability over the full range of plausible in-form, no-injury, ninety-minute scenarios — not a prediction of a scoreline.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Switzerland to win at 48%, the draw at 30%, and Canada to win at 24%. Polymarket has Canada at 24%, which prices out at American odds of +317; the model has the same side at 39%. The +15.0pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Canada side that lower bound is 32% — +7.8pp clear of the market's 24%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. The claim is narrow: on this fixture, on this side, the price is below what the underlying read supports. We don't argue the market is broadly wrong — across the priced field the model and the line agree more often than they disagree. We surface the ones where they don't.

The read above is the most recent one, not a frozen call. With kickoff 29 days out, refresh is weekly; daily cadence picks up inside the final five days. Injury news, the actual XI, and conditions at kickoff all change what the model sees. We re-publish on every refresh. The page shows what the engine reads; what to do with that information is a reader's call.
drivers: Pre-match Elo gives Canada a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +15.0pp gap clears the Desk's 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
This is a selection call on the Canada side, not a blanket read on the market.
Confirmed XI, fitness news, and weather re-enter the prior closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: A +15.0pp gap across model and market on the Canada side. Our Elo prior, after host and altitude adjustments, rates Canada at 39%; Polymarket sits at 24%.
copy.title: Switzerland v Canada · the model leans Canada
